title.en: Money and exchange (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en:
Long ago a farmer wanted a clay pot. The potter wanted rice. So the farmer gave rice for the pot.
But once the potter did not need rice that day, so no trade happened.
"If only we had something everyone accepts!" sighed the farmer.

Long ago people exchanged goods for goods. This is called barter. Barter is difficult because you must find someone who has what you need and wants what you have.
Money solves this problem. Everyone accepts it, so we can sell goods for money and buy what we want with it. Early money included shells, metal pieces and coins.
Today we use coins and notes issued by the Reserve Bank of India, and also digital payments through phones and cards. Money must be earned, saved and spent wisely.
Barter means exchanging goods for goods. It is hard to find someone who wants what you have.
Money is accepted by everyone, so trade becomes easy.
Early money was shells and metal coins. Today we use notes, coins and digital payments.
Money should be earned, saved and spent wisely.

problem.en: Why is money better than barter?

text.en: In barter you need someone who wants what you have.
With money you sell for money first.
Then you buy what you need. So trade is easier.

prompt.en: A friend says money is only coins and notes. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: Money also includes digital payments by phone and card.
It is anything everyone accepts for payment.

points.en: Barter is goods for goods and is difficult.
Money is accepted by everyone and makes trade easy.
Money can be coins, notes or digital.
